bridge: Builds on S06 least privilege and C06 kernel mediation.
teaching:
Authority is what a component is allowed to do, such as read one file or open a network connection. Ambient authority is access it gets automatically from its environment rather than a narrowly supplied object. A handle or descriptor is an operating-system-managed reference through which a process can use an opened resource. Giving a parser one read-only input handle is narrower than giving it access to your whole home directory.

Privilege separation divides a system so a failure in one component has limited authority. Identify which component genuinely needs each capability. A parser that handles untrusted text may not need network access, personal files or the ability to launch programs.

A sandbox constrains a process under a platform-specific policy. Capabilities can grant access to particular objects rather than broad ambient authority. The boundary must cover inherited handles, mounts, environment and communication channels; starting a process with a low-privilege name alone does not establish confinement.

Design a narrow interface between privileged and unprivileged parts. Validate requests at the privileged side and keep the protocol small. A helper that accepts arbitrary file paths or commands may recreate the authority you tried to remove. Test legitimate work and denied operations separately.

Split a privileged service by authority, not merely into multiple files. A logger may need append-only access to one log; a parser may need no filesystem authority; a broker may expose one narrowly authorised operation. Define allowed callers, object selection, input shape and failure behaviour at each message boundary. A fixed SQL template prevents syntax injection only when values are bound correctly; it still needs caller/object checks.

A descriptor integer names an entry in that process’s kernel-managed table. Guessing another integer cannot grant an unopened file, but an inherited or deliberately passed handle can carry real authority. Close unneeded handles before untrusted work. Plain chroot changes path resolution; it is not a complete sandbox and does not revoke existing descriptors or other powers. Software fault isolation similarly relies on the validator and trusted runtime enforcing exact invariants; it does not prove the isolated program is benevolent or cannot exhaust resources.
example:
Design fixture: document renderer
Untrusted renderer: read one supplied input; write one output directory.
Denied: network, home directory, subprocess launch.
Privileged broker: choose input/output handles; validate size and result.
Interface: render(document_id), not run(command) or read(any_path).
Expected ordinary case: render synthetic note successfully.
explanation: The broker decides which object handles the renderer receives. If it passes an unrestricted directory handle or accepts arbitrary paths, the interface may leak broader access. A successful render proves functionality, while denied-access checks provide evidence for selected confinement properties.
exercise: For the renderer fixture, list assets, allowed operations and five denied operations. Define one positive test and three harmless negative tests you would perform in the supported lab. Label paper expectations separately from observed results.
solution: Allowed work: read the supplied synthetic document and write its result in the designated output area. Five denials: read unrelated synthetic files; write outside the output area; make network connections; launch subprocesses; request another user’s document through the broker. Positive plan: render the supplied note and check expected output. Three harmless lab checks can attempt access to a disposable unrelated file, a forbidden loopback connection, and creation outside the output area; each should be denied under the chosen policy. These remain expectations until tested in the supported lab. A denied filesystem test does not by itself verify network or broker policy.
challenge: A helper runs with broad file access and exposes copy(source,destination) to an untrusted renderer. Explain how this undermines separation and redesign the interface around explicit object authority.
challenge_solution: Arbitrary source/destination paths let the renderer direct privileged operations. Replace them with validated object IDs or pre-opened constrained handles, limit output destinations and enforce caller/context rules in the broker.
